messages:
alice: Kicking off a benchmix to compare our replay harness vs the synthetic generator for KV-warmup + adaptive batching. Need fair side-by-side metrics for latency, cost, and quality. Can people run with their usual infra and drop results here?

benj: What test matrix are we using (model, seq len distro, quant profiles)?

alice: Matrix posted below — keep it narrow to reduce variance:
- model: redwood/llm-base-8k
- seq buckets: 64/256/1024 (ratios 50/35/15)
- quant: fp16, int8-static
- routing: default kernel selector v2.1 vs fallback v2.0
- kv: warmup off / warmup on (threshold 8)

carlos: Noted a perf regression in nightly after the kernel-selector change — p95 spikes when KV cache is cold. Quick log excerpt: 
```
[2028-06-02T11:12:03Z] request=abc123 kernel=kernel_proto_v2 dispatch_ms=4 kv_lookup_ms=12 batch_coalesce_ms=6 total_ms=160 -> p95 went +18ms
```

maya: Can we run both harnesses with identical session/key reuse distributions? Replay should be able to mimic hot-key locality, synth needs to be tuned. I'll try kv prewarm toggles and report.

tzhao: First pass numbers (short run, 30k tokens) — replay vs synth (matched session distro):
```
replay: tokens/s=3200, p50=32ms, p95=150ms, topk-match=0.842
synth:  tokens/s=2800, p50=34ms, p95=158ms, topk-match=0.854
```
Replay shows better throughput but slightly lower topk-match (sampling noise?). Will extend.

infra-bot: deploybot: kernel-proto v2.1 rolled to staging (image: registry/redwood/kernel:2.1) by @deploy-bot :information_source:

benj: Hmm, that log + tzhao numbers smell like different kernel selection patterns. Synth might be producing more long-tail batches or different key reuse. We should align batch-size distribution and KV hit-rate between runs.

alice: Agreed. Use this harness command to force matching distributions and tags: 
```
./benchmix --trace=replay.trace --match-dist=sessions.json --out=/tmp/benchmix-results/1839123456 --tags=kv_hit,kernel_v
./benchmix --gen=synth.profile --match-dist=sessions.json --out=/tmp/benchmix-results/1839123456/synth --tags=kv_hit,kernel_v
```

carlos: Pulled a short pprof/flame summary from an offending run. Top hotspots: kernel_dispatch, kv_lookup_hotpath, batch_coalesce. Flame excerpt: 
```
30% kernel_dispatch
18% kv_lookup_hotpath
12% batch_coalesce
6% memcopy_warmup
```

maya: Proposal for a regression gate for this benchmix: p95 latency delta <= 5% AND cost/token delta <= 6% AND quality (topk-match) delta <= 2%. Also include quantization sweeps (fp16 vs int8-static) and speculative decoding on/off. If any metric outside gate -> block kernel-proto rollout.

tzhao: Quick note: speculative decoding on synth gave ~6% latency improvement but ~0.9% topk-match drop on the short run. Might be acceptable but should be gated when combined with int8.

benj: Plan of action: run 3 sweeps across the same matched distro:
1) replay baseline (kernel v2.0)
2) synth with matched distro (kernel v2.0)
3) synth + speculative + int8 + kernel v2.1
Capture lat/cost/quality, kv hit-rate, kernel selection breakdown. Results dir: /tmp/benchmix-results/1839123456.

alice: Please annotate traces with kv_hit boolean and kernel_v string so we can slice by hit/miss and kernel. Example tagging above. Also capture per-request kernel decision trace.

sre-bot: Scheduled: inference-bench-3 cluster reserved at 2028-06-03T03:00:00Z for benchmix run (job id: bench-1839123456).

carlos: I'll collect full pprof dumps and produce HTML flamegraphs. If p95 regresses >5% on kernel v2.1 vs v2.0 for matched runs I'll raise an immediate rollback.

alice: Great. After runs, paste a single CSV with columns: run, kernel_v, kv_hit_rate, tokens_s, p50_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_k_token, topk_match. We'll collate and produce a short README with verdict. :thumbsup:
